added: (11/04/2026) Introduction This topic contains information on shared appreciation transactions, including:

The lender of the first lien mortgage may advance the funds for the shared appreciation loan if within six months of loan closing the lender assigns the loan to a housing finance agency as defined in 23 C.F.R. §266.5.

Fannie Mae will purchase first lien mortgages that are originated with this type of subordinate financing, but the first lien mortgage must be a purchase or limited cash-out refinance transaction and otherwise meet the requirements of this Guide.

The following table provides additional eligibility requirements for shared appreciation loans. ✓ Requirements The shared appreciation loan must comply with the requirements in B5-5.1-01, Community Seconds.

Expenses or fees must not be imposed on the borrower after loan origination, except in cases of default or in connection with borrower-initiated transactions, as defined in the program's legal documentation.

After completion of the obligations to the shared appreciation provider (or its assignee), including payment of any shared appreciation in value, the borrower must not have any further obligation to the shared appreciation provider or any assignee.
• a specific date, which must not be earlier than the scheduled maturity date of the first lien mortgage granted in connection with the purchase of the property;
• repayment in full of the first lien mortgage (except when the shared appreciation loan is being resubordinated in connection with a refinance);

• acceleration of the first lien mortgage in accordance with its terms (for purchase mortgages only, this is limited to acceleration after the conclusion of loss mitigation or other measures to cure a delinquency); or

If the shared appreciation loan becomes due and payable, all amounts then due and payable to the first lien mortgagee must be paid first, followed by other entitled parties, such as the shared appreciation provider and the borrower.
• the principal portion of all payments the borrower made on the first lien mortgage.

added: Overview Review of Community Seconds Programs Eligible Community Seconds Providers Acceptable Uses Additional Eligibility Requirements Rural Development Section 502 Leveraged (Blended) Loan Program Minimum Borrower Contribution Requirements Repayment Structure Pricing and Delivery Considerations Overview A Community Seconds loan is subordinate financing that is originated under an affordable housing program.

Fannie Mae does not purchase Community Seconds loans; however, first lien mortgages that are originated with this type of subordinate financing are eligible for purchase by Fannie Mae in accordance with the requirements of this Guide.
The Community Seconds Checklist is a job aid that lenders may use to support their review.
It aligns with the requirements in this Guide.
Confirm the provider of the Community Seconds loan is an eligible Community Seconds provider.
Determine the mortgage for the Community Seconds loan is clearly subordinate to the first lien mortgage.
The title insurance in effect must ensure priority of the first lien mortgage over any recorded instrument securing the Community Seconds loan.
Confirm the program allows the holder of the first lien mortgage to foreclose and acquire title to the property free and clear of all interests of the Community Seconds provider.

Eligible Community Seconds Providers A Community Seconds loan must only be funded by one of the following entities: a federal agency; a state, county, or similar political subdivisions of a state (including a housing finance agency1 ), or local government2 , so long as the first lien mortgage is secured by a residence located within the jurisdictional boundaries thereof; a nonprofit organization exempt from taxation under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code; a regional Federal Home Loan Bank under one of its affordable housing programs; an employer where a borrower is an employee (s…
Note:

In order to be an eligible Community Seconds provider, any separate legal entity (other than a nonprofit organization exempt from taxation under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code) owned directly or indirectly, in whole or in part, by a federally recognized tribe must be a TDHE (and the Community Seconds loan must satisfy the conditions applicable to a TDHE, including that the residence is located within the tribe's applicable territorial limitations or a borrower is a member of the tribe).

A corporation or other legal entity created by or owned in whole or in part by such an Indian tribe is not eligible unless it qualifies as a Tribally Designated Housing Entity, as defined in 25 U.S.C. §4103(22).
A Community Seconds provider must not be the property seller or other interested party in the transaction, except when they are the provider of a shared equity program or sweat equity program.
See B3-4.1-02, Interested Party Contributions (IPCs), B5-5.3-03, Shared Equity Transactions:
Eligibility, Underwriting and Collateral Requirements, and B5-6-02, HomeReady Mortgage Underwriting Methods and Requirements.

Acceptable Uses A Community Seconds loan must only be used to fund one or more of the following: all or part of the down payment, provided the Community Seconds loan is not funded in any way through the first lien mortgage such as premium pricing; closing costs; renovations to the property (including resiliency or energy-related improvements); or a permanent interest rate buydown.

In some cases, a Community Seconds loan may not involve the advancement of funds but instead may facilitate affordability through a subsidized sales price and/or requirements related to the future sale of the home.

The eligible provider may secure a Community Seconds loan against the property in an amount representing the difference between the market value and reduced sales price accepted by the seller (referred to as the subsidy).
The subordinate loan may also enforce requirements that prevent the borrower from selling the property outside of the confines of the program.
The terms of the loan may not, however, restrict the sale of the property upon foreclosure or acceptance of a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure except as permitted in this Guide.

When a sales price subsidy is provided and the property has resale restrictions that limit both income eligibility and impose a maximum resale price, the lender may use the Affordable LTV calculation described in B5-5.3-03, Shared Equity Transactions:
Eligibility, Underwriting and Collateral Requirements.
Additional Eligibility Requirements The following table provides additional eligibility requirements for the first lien mortgage purchased by Fannie Mae in connection with a Community Seconds loan.

Criteria Requirements First lien mortgage eligibility The first lien mortgage must be fixed-rate or an ARM with an initial fixed-rate period of five years or more, and otherwise comply with this Guide.
Maximum LTV and CLTV ratios The maximum LTV is based on the first lien mortgage LTV requirement.

The maximum CLTV is 105% with a Community Seconds loan, unless the first lien mortgage has an independent CLTV cap (such as the CLTV cap for manufactured housing that does not meet MH Advantage requirements).
Refer to the Eligibility Matrix for additional information.
Loan purpose The transaction is limited to a purchase or limited cash-out refinance.
For a limited cash-out refinance, the Community Seconds mortgage holder must acknowledge their lien position by executing a resubordination agreement.
The agreement must be recorded to ensure enforceability.
Property and occupancy The subject property must be a one- to four-unit principal residence.
If the loan is secured by a manufactured home, it must comply with all manufactured home policies including LTV and CLTV ratio requirements.
Income limits If income limits are imposed by both the Community Seconds provider and the first lien mortgage, the more restrictive will apply.
Note:
Loans secured by community land trusts properties and properties with income and resale price restrictions have additional requirements.
See B5-5.3-03, Shared Equity Transactions:
Eligibility, Underwriting and Collateral Requirements.

Rural Development Section 502 Leveraged (Blended) Loan Program A subordinate lien originated in connection with a conventional first lien mortgage under the RD Section 502 Leveraged (Blended) Loan Program is eligible for the Community Seconds program.
The standard review of Community Seconds programs described in B5-5.1-01, Community Seconds, is not required; however, the subordinate lien must meet all RD Guidelines.
See B6-1-05, Eligible RD-Guaranteed Mortgages for additional information.
